sam_dev: Hey — I pip installed the SDK but `import redwood` raises ModuleNotFoundError. Installed with `pip install redwood-inference` on macOS.

sam_dev: Command I ran:
```
pip install redwood-inference
python -c \"import redwood; print(redwood.__version__)\"
```
Traceback:
```
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'redwood'
```

lee_support: Sorry about the trouble — can you paste `python --version`, `pip --version`, and `python -m pip show redwood-inference`?

sam_dev: Sure:
```
$ python --version
Python 3.11.2
$ pip --version
pip 23.1.2 from /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/pip (python 3.10)
$ python -m pip show redwood-inference
Name: redwood-inference
Version: 0.12.1
Location: /usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages
```

sam_dev: But `which python` -> `/Users/sam/.pyenv/versions/3.11.2/bin/python` so looks like pip is tied to system python while I'm running pyenv python.

maria_eng: That mismatch is the usual culprit. Try installing with the interpreter you actually run: `python -m pip install --force-reinstall redwood-inference` (using the pyenv python). Also check `echo $PYTHONPATH` in case you have site packages forced.

sam_dev: Ran that, but still `ModuleNotFoundError`. I also noticed `export PYTHONPATH=/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages:$PYTHONPATH` in my .bash_profile from an old guide.

lee_support: Ah — that will cause the wrong site-packages to be picked up. Do `unset PYTHONPATH` or remove that line, then reinstall in the pyenv env. Also check for .egg-link and .pth files in both site-packages dirs.

sam_dev: Found `redwood_inference.egg-link` in `/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages` pointing to an old dev checkout. I removed it and reinstalled with the pyenv python:
```
/Users/sam/.pyenv/versions/3.11.2/bin/python -m pip install --force-reinstall --no-cache-dir redwood-inference==0.12.1
```

sysbot: :white_check_mark: Package redwood-inference 0.12.1 installed in /Users/sam/.pyenv/versions/3.11.2/lib/python3.11/site-packages

sam_dev: After that `import redwood` works. Looks like a mix of PYTHONPATH + leftover egg-link was shadowing the correct package. Thanks.

maria_eng: Glad it worked. For reproducibility: prefer `python -m venv` or pyenv-virtualenv, avoid global PYTHONPATH, and use `python -m pip` to ensure pip matches the interpreter.

sam_dev: Will do. Closing this thread. :thumbsup:
